definitions.gloss: New Year decorations; New Year's ornaments
definitions.explanation: Traditional decorations displayed in homes and businesses around the Japanese New Year to welcome the year deity ({年神|としがみ}) and bring good fortune.

examples.japanese: {正月飾|しょうがつかざ}り⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飾|かざ}った→飾る：01185_kazaru⟧。
examples.english: I put up New Year decorations.

examples.japanese: ⟦{十二月|じゅうにがつ}→十二月：00636_juunigatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、{正月飾|しょうがつかざ}り⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{並|なら}び→並ぶ：00605_narabu⟧{始|はじ}める。
examples.english: In December, New Year decorations start appearing in stores.

examples.japanese: {松|まつ}の{内|うち}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{過|す}ぎたら→過ぎる：01219_sugiru⟧、{正月飾|しょうがつかざ}り⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{外|はず}して→外す：02394_hazusu⟧⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{持|も}っていく→持っていく：27431_motteiku⟧。
examples.english: After the New Year period ends, we take down the decorations and bring them to a shrine.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{正月|しょうがつ}→正月：01433_shougatsu⟧ (New Year) + ⟦{飾|かざ}り→飾り：02539_kazari⟧ (decoration). A collective term for the various decorations used during the Japanese New Year season.

TYPES:
- ⟦{門松|かどまつ}→門松：14522_kadomatsu⟧: pine decorations placed at gates/entrances
- ⟦{鏡餅|かがみもち}→鏡餅：19469_kagamimochi⟧: stacked rice cakes as an offering
- {注連飾|しめかざ}り: sacred rope decoration for doorways

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {正月飾|しょうがつかざ}り⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飾|かざ}る→飾る：01185_kazaru⟧: to put up New Year decorations
- {正月飾|しょうがつかざ}り⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{外|はず}す→外す：02394_hazusu⟧: to take down New Year decorations
- {正月飾|しょうがつかざ}り⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}う→買う：00489_kau⟧: to buy New Year decorations

CULTURAL NOTE:
Decorations are typically put up by December 28 — setting them up on December 29 ({二重苦|にじゅうく}, double suffering) or December 31 ({一夜飾|いちやかざ}り, one-night decoration) is considered unlucky. They are removed after {松|まつ}の{内|うち} (usually January 7) and burned at a shrine ceremony called どんど{焼|や}き.
